answer: Each applicant finishes a sequential proof-of-work voyage: step k hashes step k-1, so one machine cannot shortcut the chain, and a verifier checks the path before issuing a non-transferable trellis credential bound to one key. That credential is locked in a vault requiring a short new segment each epoch; a second key presenting the same credential is rejected. Extra identities repeat the voyage separately, so n identities cost nL work and total gain is n(R-cL). Deterrence holds only while R<cL; rented machines keep cost linear.
